reading.title: Чтение
reading.about: 3 текста разной сложности, по 4 вопроса к каждому. Можно перечитывать текст сколько угодно.

parts.title: Текст 1 · Сообщение в рабочем чате
parts.passage:
Hi everyone,

From Monday 9 November the office on the third floor will be closed for repairs for two weeks. During this time, the design team will work on the fifth floor, in the meeting room next to the kitchen.

Please take your laptops home on Friday evening — there will be no space to leave them. The coffee machine on the fifth floor is broken, but a new one will arrive on Tuesday.

If you would rather work from home during the repairs, tell your manager by Thursday.

Thanks,
Marta

items.q: How long will the repairs take?
Where will the design team work?
options: In a meeting room on the fifth floor

items.q: What should people do on Friday evening?
Working from home during the repairs is…
options: possible if you tell your manager by Thursday

parts.title: Текст 2 · Статья о дизайнере
parts.passage:
When Lena started her first job as a product designer, she avoided talking to developers. She was worried they would ask technical questions she couldn't answer.

After a difficult project in which several of her screens had to be redesigned at the last minute, she decided to change her approach. She didn't try to become a programmer; instead, she spent an hour a week learning the basics of how web pages are built.

Within a few months, she noticed that her conversations with developers had become shorter and more productive. She could predict which ideas would be expensive to build and suggest simpler alternatives early.

"The biggest change wasn't technical," she says. "It was that developers started inviting me to their planning meetings." Today Lena recommends that every junior designer spend a little time on the basics — not to write code, but to understand the people who do.

items.q: Why did Lena avoid developers at first?
options: She was afraid of technical questions

items.q: What made her change her approach?
options: A project where screens had to be redone late

items.q: What was her main aim in learning the basics?
options: To understand how web pages are built

items.q: According to Lena, the most important result was that…
options: developers began to include her in planning

parts.title: Текст 3 · Статья о концентрации
parts.passage:
Most people believe that they are good at multitasking, but research suggests otherwise. What we call multitasking is usually rapid switching between tasks, and every switch carries a cost: it takes time for the brain to fully re-engage with the previous task.

For short, routine activities this cost is barely noticeable. For complex work, such as writing or designing, it can add up to a significant loss of time and quality.

Interestingly, the problem is not only the interruptions themselves but the expectation of them. Some studies suggest that people perform worse when they merely know a message might arrive, even if it never does.

This has led some companies to experiment with "quiet hours" — fixed periods when no meetings are scheduled and chat notifications are paused. Early results are encouraging, although critics point out that such policies only work if managers follow them too; otherwise, employees feel they must stay available anyway.

items.q: What does the writer say about multitasking?
options: It is mostly switching quickly between tasks
It improves the quality of work
Most people are good at it

items.q: The cost of switching is most serious for…
According to the text, performance can drop when people…
options: only expect that a message may arrive

items.q: What is the critics' point about quiet hours?
options: They only work if managers respect them as well

listening.title: Аудирование
listening.about: 3 части: короткие фразы, диалог, выступление. Слушайте сколько угодно раз, но не открывайте текст — его нет.

lines.t: Hi, thanks for joining. I've had a look at the homepage designs. Overall, we really like the direction.
Great to hear. Is there anything you'd like to change?
Just one thing. Our sales team feels the pricing section is too far down the page. They'd like people to see it earlier.
That makes sense. I can move it up, but then the customer stories would drop below it. Is that okay?
Yes, that's fine. The stories are nice, but pricing is what people ask about first.
Okay. I'll send an updated version on Wednesday, and if you approve it, we can hand it off to development on Friday.

items.q: What does the client think of the designs overall?
Who wants the pricing section moved?
What will happen to the customer stories?
options: They will appear below the pricing
They will move to a separate page

items.q: When could the design go to development?
options: On Friday, if the client approves it

lines.t: Good morning, everyone. Today I want to talk about why accessibility should be part of our process from the very beginning, rather than something we check at the end.

When accessibility is left until the last stage, fixing problems usually means redesigning components that are already built, which is slow and expensive. By contrast, if we choose accessible colour combinations and clear focus states while we're still sketching, the extra effort is minimal.

There's also a common misconception that accessible design only benefits a small group of users. In reality, features like larger tap targets and good contrast help everyone — for example, someone using their phone in bright sunlight.
So my proposal is simple: we add three accessibility questions to every design review, starting next sprint.

items.q: What is the main purpose of the talk?
options: To suggest including accessibility early in the process
To report on a finished project

items.q: Why is late accessibility work a problem?
options: Built components have to be redesigned, which is slow and costly
It is not allowed in most companies

items.q: The speaker mentions bright sunlight to show that…
What exactly does the speaker propose?
options: Adding three accessibility questions to every design review

writing.title: Письмо
writing.about: 2 задания. Оценивает Claude по критериям CEFR: содержание, достижение цели, организация текста, язык. Результат придёт в следующем пакете.

parts.title: Задание 1 · Письмо коллеге (B1)
Задание 2 · Эссе-мнение (B2)
parts.prompt: Some people think that working from home makes teams less creative. Write an essay (140–190 words) giving your opinion. Support it with reasons and examples from your own experience.

speaking.title: Говорение
speaking.about: Ответьте вслух на 3 вопроса, около минуты на каждый. Потом честно отметьте, что у вас получилось — уровень посчитается по этой самооценке.

prompts.t: Talk about your job. What do you do, what do you like about it, and what is difficult?
Describe a project you are proud of. What was the problem, what did you do, and what was the result?
Some people say AI tools will replace designers. Do you agree? Give reasons and examples.

descriptors.t: Я могу простыми фразами рассказать о своей работе и дне.
Я могу задать и ответить на простые вопросы на знакомые темы.
Я могу сказать, что мне нравится и что нет.
Я могу рассказать о прошлом проекте, связывая события словами then, because, so.
Я могу высказать мнение и объяснить его простыми причинами.
Я справляюсь с обычным рабочим разговором, хотя иногда подбираю слова.
Я могу 1–2 минуты говорить на рабочую тему без долгих пауз.
Я могу объяснить плюсы и минусы разных вариантов.
Я могу участвовать в обсуждении с носителями языка и отстаивать свою точку зрения.
Я говорю свободно и спонтанно, почти не ищу слова.
Я меняю стиль речи: формально с клиентом, неформально с коллегами.
Я могу выстроить чёткую, логичную аргументацию на сложную тему.
